newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish higher on dollar strength.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish higher on dollar strength.

text.p: French stocks finished higher on Wednesday on the dollar's rise following a widely anticipated quarter-point increase in U.S. interest rates, brokers said.
An early drop on Wall Street and stronger-than-expected U.S. durable goods orders failed to brake the advance on the bourse and other European markets.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 24.48 points, or 0.93 percent, at 2,648.73, while the CAC-40 March futures contract rose 17 points to 2,644. Volume was 7.97 billion francs.
Electrical equipment supplier Schneider rose 6.26 percent to 320.70 francs on better than expected results.
Its 1996 net attributable profit surged 61.6 percent to 1.32 billion francs. The market was anticipating a 1996 profit of around 1.25 billion.

Chairman Didier Pineau-Valencienne said the company was studying ways of reducing its equity capital, possibly through a share buyback, to boost earnings per share. He also said he expected a "significant improvement" in 1997 results.

Renault shares rose 4.37 percent to 148 francs. Its truck unit said on Wednesday that it expected a narrower loss for 1997. It said it expected to break even in the second half of next year. "That was very good news," a broker said.
He said it was a good sign, technically, that the stock had broken above 144 francs. "That opens the way to 165 francs," the price at which the carmaker was partly privatised in late 1994.
Shares in Pinault-Printemps-Redoute rose 2.45 percent to 2,302 francs ahead of its results. After the close, it posted a profit of 2.07 billion francs, up from 1.52 billion.
Oil exploration equipment firm Coflexip shares rose 5.49 percent to 346 francs. It reported a profit of 76 million francs, compared with a 1995 loss of 102 million.
Canal Plus shares rose 3.19 percent to 1,166 francs on its valuations of Nethold and Telepiu pay TV assets.
